BiblicalUsage: Bariy means fat, well-fed, plump. It is the word for Pharaoh's fat cows that come up out of the river and are eaten by the lean ones, for the fat sheep the shepherds of Israel feed on while the flock starves, and for Daniel and his friends, who look fairer and fatter in flesh than all the young men who ate the king's meat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fatness in Scripture cuts both ways, because Pharaoh's fat cows are eaten and the fat shepherds are judged, while Daniel's health is the fruit of obedience. The difference is never the food; it is whether the fatness came from trusting God or from feeding on His people.
